note: Ten fictional module inputs about a made-up product (Pawpath, appointment software for independent vet clinics, by the made-up Fernway Labs). No real companies, people or brands. Rubric expectations (required sections, framework markers) were written before any model run. Regexes are case-insensitive and are matched against the markdown output (headings, bold labels or table headers all count).

required.label: executive summary
required.note: Heading such as Executive Summary / Summary / TL;DR, OR (as the prompt literally asks for "a one-paragraph executive summary") a prose paragraph of 300+ characters between the H1 and the first ## heading. Widened after the one-module smoke run, which had the paragraph but no heading.

sections.label: Problem Statement
sections.value: Clinics using Pawpath lose follow-up visits: 31% of patients due for a recheck never rebook. Front-desk staff spend about 6 hours a week on reminder calls. Rebooking today needs a phone call.

sections.label: Target Users
sections.value: Pet owners with a recheck due, and front-desk staff at independent clinics with 2 to 8 vets. 74% of owners open Pawpath reminders on a phone.

sections.label: Goals & Success Metrics
sections.value: Raise recheck rebooking from 69% to 80% within two quarters. Cut reminder-call time from 6 to 2 hours a week per clinic.

sections.label: Scope & Constraints
sections.value: In scope: one-tap rebooking from SMS and email reminders. Out of scope: payments. Must reuse the existing Pawpath calendar service. 10 weeks to beta with 12 pilot clinics.

framework.label: user stories in 'As a ... I want ... so' form
framework.note: Allows the story to wrap across lines (widened after the run; the first version required one line).

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Fernway Labs sells Pawpath to independent vet clinics. 410 paying clinics today, $1.9M ARR. Monthly logo churn is 2.1%. Most churn happens in the first 90 days.

sections.label: Goals & Objectives
sections.value: Grow paying clinics. Cut early churn. Make onboarding self-serve so sales can focus on multi-site groups.

sections.label: Constraints & Considerations
sections.value: Team: 9 engineers, 2 designers, 3 onboarding specialists. No paid acquisition budget increase in H2.

framework.label: outcomes vs outputs or sandbagging addressed

sections.label: Key Inputs
sections.value: Eight interviews with clinic managers who switched to Pawpath in the last year. Common quotes: 'Our phones never stopped ringing', 'Double bookings embarrassed us in front of clients', 'I wanted my evenings back'. Six of eight had used a paper diary plus a shared spreadsheet before.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Pawpath is appointment software for independent vet clinics. The team wants to sharpen messaging and the onboarding flow.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Pawpath is moving SMS reminders to a new messaging vendor in 6 weeks. 410 clinics send about 180,000 reminders a month. The old vendor contract ends on 30 November.

sections.label: Key Inputs
sections.value: The new vendor has not been load-tested above 20,000 messages an hour. Clinics in two regions need sender-ID registration that takes 3 to 4 weeks. Support tickets about missed reminders doubled last month.

sections.label: Constraints & Considerations
sections.value: Cannot extend the old contract. One engineer owns messaging.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Pawpath earns a flat monthly fee per clinic. Clinics that confirm at least 80% of appointments through Pawpath reminders renew at a much higher rate than those that do not. Today 52% of booked appointments are confirmed through Pawpath.

sections.label: Goals & Objectives
sections.value: Pick one metric that reflects value delivered to clinics and pet owners, and the levers the team can move.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Pawpath is appointment and reminder software for independent vet clinics with 2 to 8 vets. Clinics today use paper diaries, generic booking tools built for salons, or the scheduling module inside large practice-management suites.

sections.label: Key Inputs
sections.value: Unique attributes: species-aware visit lengths, recheck reminders tied to the treatment given, and a setup that takes one afternoon. Customers say the reminders are the reason they stay.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Pawpath sends recheck reminders 3 days before the due date. Rebooking rate from reminders is 69%. Hypothesis from support: reminders sent 7 days before give owners more time to plan.

sections.label: Key Inputs
sections.value: About 24,000 recheck reminders are sent per month across 410 clinics. Clinics vary a lot in size.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: When a slot is cancelled, clinics phone owners on a paper waitlist. Pawpath wants an automatic waitlist that offers freed slots by SMS.

sections.label: Key Inputs
sections.value: Users: pet owners, front-desk staff, clinic managers. A freed slot should be offered to the first matching owner and held for 15 minutes.

sections.value: Pawpath: 410 independent vet clinics, $1.9M ARR, strong reminder feature, small team of 14. No integrations with lab systems yet. Two large practice-management suites are bundling basic scheduling for free.

sections.value: Decide where to invest in H2.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Pawpath sells to independent vet clinics with 2 to 8 vets in one country. Price is $390 per clinic per month. Fernway's own CRM lists about 6,200 such clinics in its home country, of which an estimated 70% do not use a dedicated scheduling tool.

sections.label: Goals & Objectives
sections.value: Size the opportunity for the board. Be explicit about assumptions.
